name: relay-bypass
title: Relay true bypass with a photo-MOS mute
about: True bypass with a DPDT signal relay (HFD4/5, gold-plated contacts): coil off is bypass – in to out directly, the effect's input on ground; coil on routes in to fx_in and fx_out to out. An S8050 drives the coil from a logic signal, an SS14 takes its switch-off spike. A PhotoMOS (AQY212GS, 0.7 Ω) shorts the output to ground while the contacts move, so the switching does not click. Pull-downs hold every contact at 0 V DC. Maker-coverage BL-18.

ports.ctl: the relay drive from the MCU: high = effect on
ports.mute: the mute from the MCU: high = output shorted to ground
ports.vplus: the coil's supply: a 5 V rail

components.label: {as}: bypass relay DPDT, 5 V coil, gold contacts
components.notes: Set 1 (common 3): out to in (NC 2, bypass) or to fx_out (NO 4). Set 2 (common 6): fx_in to in (NO 5) or to ground (NC 7).

nets.name: in
nets.notes: The input jack: R4 2.2 MΩ in bypass, with R5 1.1 MΩ while the effect is on – plus what out or fx_in carry.

notes: Coil off = bypass: without power, or before the firmware runs (R2 holds Q1 off), the signal passes from in to out. A latching relay would keep its last state when power is lost (maker-coverage GTP 31). Set 2 grounds the effect's input while bypassed.

K1 HFD4/5: AgNi + Au plated contacts for signal levels (maker-coverage GTI 31); coil 178 Ω, 28 mA at 5 V, pick-up 3.75 V max, release 0.5 V min. vplus is a 5 V rail – the regulator that feeds the MCU counts the coil (GTI 30). The coil endures 10 V only for a short time: on a 9 V rail directly the HFD4/9 (579 Ω, 6.75 V pick-up) instead.

Q1 S8050 with R1 1 kΩ and R2 10 kΩ: about 2.5 mA base current from a 3.3 V pin for 28 mA of coil current – saturated (hFE ≥ 200). D1 SS14 across the coil, cathode at vplus, takes the switch-off spike (REQ.missing); it makes the release slower than the 3 ms of the data sheet.

OK1 AQY212GS across out: Ron 0.7 Ω max at IF 5 mA. R3 330 Ω gives (3.3 V − 1.14 V) / 330 Ω = 6.5 mA from a 3.3 V pin, 11.5 mA from 5 V – inside the 5–30 mA it recommends; the MCU pin must allow it (Pico 2: 12 mA).

Mute window in the firmware: mute on; after ≥ 5 ms (OK1's turn-on at 5 mA, max) switch the relay; after ≥ 3 ms (K1's operate or release, max – longer with D1) plus the contacts' bounce, mute off (OK1 turns off within 0.5 ms). mstratman/relay-bypass mutes 35 ms in all (maker-coverage BL-18).

R4, R5 2.2 MΩ and R6 100 kΩ: every contact at 0 V DC in every state, so switching does not click (REQ.value/switch). R6 discharges the effect's output capacitor. The guitar sees R4 (2.2 MΩ) in bypass and R4 ∥ R5 (1.1 MΩ) with the effect on – each time in parallel with the amplifier or the effect's input. The effect's input and output must be DC-free (coupling capacitors, as in block instrument-buffer).
OK1's output capacitance (up to about 220 pF at 0 V, typical) loads out in bypass like a short cable.
K1's minimum applicable load, 10 mV 10 µA, is a reference value; a guitar into 1 MΩ carries about 1 µA – Hongfa's (825) version is for tiny loads.

The simulation switches K1's first contact set only (the relay kind has one set of roles): with the relay on, in reaches fx_in only on the board – an AC run from in to out shows nothing then; run it from fx_in or fx_out to out instead, and from in to out in bypass. OK1's MOSFET output has no model (the optocoupler kind's output is a transistor) – it is open there. R4 and R5 give set 2's nets their level in the simulation as on the board.
sim.json: ctl and mute under the MCU's outputs; a load with ctl high and "relays_on": [<K>], a load with mute high – REQ.value/switch holds every contact on signal nets at one DC level in each.

test.about: in, out, fx_in and fx_out become T_IN, T_OUT, T_FX_IN and T_FX_OUT – the effect is left out; the relay is K1, the PhotoMOS OK1
